title: Flash-onset US county droughts ended 8 weeks sooner than gradual-onset droughts after first D2 (USDM, 2000-2026); precipitation did not explain it, and it gave no forecast gain after 2012
abstract: Question: after a U.S. county first reaches severe drought (D2) in the U.S. Drought Monitor, does a fast onset predict a shorter remaining drought, and does precipitation explain it? Approach: we built 24,784 county drought events (CONUS, 2000-2026) from weekly USDM county statistics. Flash onset means D0 or better to D2 in 4 weeks or less (13,910 events). Gradual onset means 9 weeks or more (4,091 events). We measured weeks from the first D2 map to the end of drought. We added SPI-like indices from CPC daily gauge precipitation and used Kaplan-Meier medians, stratified Cox models and a calendar-year block bootstrap. Results: flash-onset droughts ended sooner (median 15 vs 23 weeks; difference 8, 95% interval 4-12; hazard ratio of drought end 1.22, 1.12-1.33). Peak severity was similar. Median duration increased steadily with onset weeks. Post-onset precipitation was the same in both classes. Adding it raised the hazard ratio to 1.34. Antecedent precipitation at onset did not change it (1.21). 91-day precipitation returned to normal after 14 weeks in both classes, but the USDM removed flash droughts sooner after that (7 vs 12 weeks). Gradual droughts had 365-day deficits that recovered 12 weeks later. The effect held within region x year x season strata (1.22) and under four definition changes (1.19-1.24). It was weaker in 2013-2026 (1.13, 0.99-1.27). It was regional: strongest in the South and Southeast, reversed in the Upper Midwest and Southwest. Onset speed gave no out-of-sample gain for forecasting drought longer than 26 weeks in 2013-2026 (Brier change +0.0001, -0.0014 to +0.0016). Limitations: the USDM is an expert blend whose practice changed. We used no soil moisture, streamflow or temperature data, so we cannot separate physical storage from depiction memory. Several checks were added after the first results.
